newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 24.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Korea High Speed Railway Construction Authority's ex-chief said the Ministry of Construction & Transportation and the authority hid part of the WJE's report in April on the safety of the Seoul-Pusan high speed rail. WJE is a private U.S. company hired by the ex-chief to inspect the safety of the construction.

- The government will not extend loans to save the financially troubled Kia Group as it goes against the World Trade Organisation's agreement which bans governments from supporting a specific company, finance minister Kang Kyong-shik reported to President Kim Young-sam.
- Real estate prices are expected to plunge as large conglomerates in financial trouble scurry to sell their properties to raise funds.
- The Ministry of Information & Communication plans to raise local call charges by 8.2 percent and public telephone charges by 25 percent.

- Opposition parties have renewed their attack against the ruling party in the National Assembly by demanding that President Kim Young-sam reveal his spending during the 1992 presidential election campaign.

- Top managers of the Kia Group are planning to give up the management rights and the group's executives and emplotees will hand over their shares in Kia Motors and other Kia affiliates to creditors, bowing to the demands of creditor banks.
